```{r loading packages and data}
first_collection<- read_excel("Anonymized_Data/full_first_collection.xlsx")
column_clean_names<- read.csv("first_collection_cols_clean.csv")
```

```{r data clean}

first_collection_clean<-clean_names(first_collection)

#Keeping only the people who submitted the questionnaire, and manageing exclusions
#need to find and exclude the tests

first_collection_clean<- first_collection_clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(status=="Submitted") %>%
  dplyr::filter(does_your_child_have_any_hearing_or_vision_problems_or_developmental_delays== "No")


#Now let's select only the columns of data that we need

columns_drop<- c(2,3,4,5,7,10,11,12,15,17,20,25,26,27,28,36,37,38,39,40, 41,42,43,50,56,57,58,59,60,61,62,63,64,65,66,67,68,69,70,71,72,73,74,75,76,77,78,79,80,81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89,90,91,92,93,94,95,97,98,100,104,105,106,107,115,116,118,122,123,130,132,133,135,139,140,147,149,150,152,156,157,164,167,166,169,173,174,186,188,190,191,197,199,200,201)



first_collection_clean<- first_collection_clean%>%
  dplyr::select(-all_of(columns_drop))


# write.csv(
#   first_collection_clean,
#   here("Anonymized_Data/first_collection_clean.csv"),
#   row.names = FALSE
# )


first_collection_clean <- first_collection_clean %>%
  rename(!!!setNames(column_clean_names$old_names,
                     column_clean_names$new_names))


#Now let's get dates into the correct format 
first_collection_clean $survey_date<- as.Date(first_collection_clean $survey_date)
first_collection_clean $child_dob <- as.Date(first_collection_clean$child_dob)

#Let's make an age variable, calculated from the date of the survey and the date of birth
first_collection_clean$child_age_years <- time_length(
  interval(first_collection_clean$child_dob, first_collection_clean$survey_date),
  unit = "years"
) |> floor()

```
```{r}

#1 let's get the census division data for rate of multilingualism

qc_geo_cd <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR = "24"),
  level = "CD",
  vectors = "v_CA21_1"   # dummy vector just to retrieve geographies
) %>%
clean_names() %>%
distinct(geo_uid, region_name)

#Got the census division names and geo_uid codes so that we can easily get the info from rate of multilingualsim
#But the name of regions has wierd characters and I need it to match with the names on the survey. So fixing it.
	
qc_geo_cd <- qc_geo_cd  %>%

mutate(
census_subdivision = str_remove(region_name, "[(].*")
    ) %>%
  mutate(census_subdivision = str_remove(census_subdivision , "\\s+$")) %>%
  select(-region_name)



#Now let's pull the census division bilingualism rate
qc_cd_bilingual_rate <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR="24"),
  level = "CD",
  vectors = c(
    total = "v_CA21_1",
    bilingual = "v_CA21_436"
  ) ) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(multilingual_rate = total/ bilingual) |>
  select(geo_uid, multilingual_rate)

#let's combine information for both

cd_multilingual_rate<-qc_geo_cd %>%
  left_join(qc_cd_bilingual_rate, by="geo_uid")


#finally, let's merge it with our own data frame
first_collection_w_predictors<- first_collection_clean %>%
  left_join(cd_multilingual_rate, by="census_subdivision")


```

```{r adding density of speaker by language}
# Look for mother tongue variables

languages_heard<- first_collection_w_predictors %>%
  dplyr::select(internal_id, census_subdivision, child_english, child_french, child_first_minority, child_second_minority, child_third_minority, geo_uid) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols=child_english:child_third_minority, names_to="language_type",values_to="language") %>%
  mutate(language = case_when(
     language== "Allemand" ~ "German",
      language== "allemand" ~ "German",
      language== "Suisse-Allemand"~"German",
      language== "Espagnol" ~ "Spanish",
      language== "espagnol" ~ "Spanish",
      language== "hungarian" ~ "Hungarian",
      language== "Polonais" ~ "Polish",
      language== "polonais" ~ "Polish",
      language== "Spanish and German" ~ "German",
      language== "francaus et arabe" ~ "Arabic",
     language==  "Portugais"~ "Portuguese",
     language==  "Bosnian (Serbian, Croatian)" ~ "Bosnian",
     language==  "Grec"~ "Greek",
     language==  "Créole Reunionnais" ~ "Creole",
      language== "Créole reunionnais"~ "Creole",
     language==  "Italien"~ "Italian",
      language== "Lsq" ~ "QSL",
      language== "LSQ"~ "QSL",
     language==  "Arménien" ~ "Armenian",
      language== "Malgache"~ "Malagasy",
     language==  "Cri"~"Cree",
                              T~ language
                              ))




#let's create a list of the languages in the survey
survey_languages <- languages_heard %>%
  distinct(language) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  arrange(language)

#retreiving the census 2021 variables

ca21_vectors <- list_census_vectors("CA21")

#now let's find out what the retrieveing vector for mother toungue is in the census data

#This code below helps us get the vectorized codes to pull the languages we want to pull (I went with total)
mother_tongue_vars <- ca21_vectors %>%
  filter(
    str_detect(
      str_to_lower(label),
      "mother tongue"
    )
  )

#this code below provides the actual individual vectorized codes for each mother tongue
mother_tongue_children <- child_census_vectors(
  "v_CA21_1174",
  leaves_only = TRUE
)

#A problem is that the first few rows are counting people who speak more than one mother tongue, so I'll identify those rows.

mother_tongue_parents <- ca21_vectors %>%
  filter(
    vector %in% unique(mother_tongue_children$parent_vector)
  ) %>%
  select(vector, label, parent_vector)


multiple_response_vector <- mother_tongue_parents %>%
  filter(label == "Multiple responses") %>%
  pull(vector)

multiple_response_children <- child_census_vectors(
  multiple_response_vector,
  leaves_only = TRUE
)
#This is going to keep census data only for single language responses, since the multiple language responses are like French+non-official language, so I have no way of adjudicating the count to a specific language.
single_language_vectors <- mother_tongue_children %>%
  filter(!vector %in% multiple_response_children$vector)


#Ok now I can create a look up variable to look up for the census languages that are in my survey

language_lookup <- single_language_vectors %>%
  select(
    vector,
    census_language = label
  )

#to avoid breaking the r memory by querying too many languages at once, I will break up the query into batches

language_vectors <- language_lookup$vector

# Break vector IDs into batches of 50
vector_batches <- split(
  language_vectors,
  ceiling(seq_along(language_vectors) / 50)
)

language_batches <- lapply(
  vector_batches,
  function(x) {
    get_census(
      dataset = "CA21",
      regions = list(PR = "24"),
      level = "CD",
      vectors = x,
       labels = "short"
    )
  }
)

qc_cd_languages_wide <- language_batches[[1]]

if (length(language_batches) > 1) {
  
  for (i in 2:length(language_batches)) {
    
    new_vectors <- intersect(
      language_vectors,
      names(language_batches[[i]])
    )
    
    qc_cd_languages_wide <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
      left_join(
        language_batches[[i]] %>%
          select(GeoUID, all_of(new_vectors)),
        by = "GeoUID"
      )
  }
}


qc_cd_languages_wide <- language_batches[[1]]

for (i in 2:length(language_batches)) {

  new_cols <- setdiff(
    names(language_batches[[i]]),
    names(qc_cd_languages_wide)
  )

  qc_cd_languages_wide <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
    left_join(
      language_batches[[i]] %>%
        select(GeoUID, all_of(new_cols)),
      by = "GeoUID"
    )
}

#making the dataframe long instead of wide

census_language_cd <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("v_CA21_"),
    names_to = "vector",
    values_to = "mother_tongue_n"
  )


#joining this dataframe with the language look up

census_language_cd <- census_language_cd %>%
  left_join(
    language_lookup,
    by = "vector"
  )

#Now I have all the regions, language names, and speaker n. I will add the population denominator to be able to calculate a speaker rate or density

cd_population_mt <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR = "24"),
  level = "CD",
  vectors = "v_CA21_1174",
  labels = "short"
)


cd_population_mt <- cd_population_mt %>%
  select(
    GeoUID,
    mother_tongue_population = v_CA21_1174
  )

census_language_cd <- census_language_cd %>%
  left_join(
    cd_population_mt,
    by = "GeoUID"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    mother_tongue_rate = mother_tongue_n / mother_tongue_population,
    mother_tongue_percent = mother_tongue_rate * 100
  )

#Checking if the labels in my survey data match the cancensus language labels.
language_crosswalk <- languages_heard %>%
  distinct(language) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  rename(survey_language = language) %>%
  mutate(
    census_language = case_when(
      survey_language == "Berber" ~ "Berber languages, n.i.e.",
      TRUE ~ survey_language
    ),
    
    exact_match = census_language %in% language_lookup$census_language
  )
```
